name: Network Share Discovery
description: Adversaries may look for folders and drives shared on remote systems as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as a precursor for Collection and to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral Movement. Networks often contain shared network drives and folders that enable users to access file directories on various systems across a network. File sharing over a Windows network occurs over the SMB protocol. (Citation: Wikipedia Shared Resource) (Citation: TechNet Shared Folder) [Net](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0039) can be used to query a remote system for available shared drives using the net view \\\\remotesystem command. It can also be used to query shared drives on the local system using net share. For macOS, the sharing -l command lists all shared points used for smb services.

references.description: Microsoft. (n.d.). Share a Folder or Drive. Retrieved June 30, 2017.
Wikipedia. (2017, April 15). Shared resource. Retrieved June 30, 2017.

telemetry.name: Command Execution
telemetry.description: Execution of a command and its interpreter or parent context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect process command lines and relevant shell/interpreter audit; shell history alone is neither complete nor tamper-resistant.

providers.name: PowerShell Script Block Logging
providers.scope: Script content via event 4104 when configured; channel depends on PowerShell edition.

providers.name: Sysmon process events
providers.scope: Interpreter launch and parent context, not full script content.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: execve-family execution context; shell built-ins need additional instrumentation.

configuration: Enable Script Block Logging through the policy/configuration for the installed edition. Forward Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational for Windows PowerShell, or PowerShellCore/Operational for PowerShell 7.
Retain script-block ID and fragment ordering alongside process creation. Protect access to collected script text; secrets may be included.
On Linux, use narrowly scoped Audit execution rules for the lab account and supported architectures, and retain joined SYSCALL/EXECVE/PATH records.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Script content and process command lines are different signals. Logging may be partial, fragmented, filtered or disabled; never assume a command line reveals everything executed.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and principal: rare interpreters, command argument patterns and parent-child sequences. Normalize scripts carefully; obfuscation, administrative automation and missing command lines change visibility.

telemetry.name: Named Pipe Metadata
telemetry.description: Metadata about a named pipe and its creation or connection.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon PipeEvent 17–18 with pipe name and owning/connecting process; pipe contents require other instrumentation.

Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
Keep this Windows-specific source separate from other operating systems; there is no direct cross-platform event-ID equivalence.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Flow
telemetry.description: Connection/flow summaries such as endpoints, duration, byte counts and transport.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Zeek conn.log, Suricata flow events or exporter equivalents, including observation point and sampling settings.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

providers.name: AWS VPC Flow Logs
providers.scope: IP traffic metadata alternative; no packet payload or DNS answer history, and some traffic is not logged.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

strategies.name: Behavior-chain detection for T1135 Network Share Discovery across Windows, Linux, and macOS

analytics.name: Analytic 0513
analytics.guidance: Process or script enumerates network shares via CLI (net view/net share, PowerShell Get-SmbShare/WMI) or OS APIs (NetShareEnum/ srvsvc.NetShareEnumAll RPC) → bursts of outbound SMB/RPC connections (445/139, \\host\IPC$ / srvsvc) to many hosts inside a short window → optional follow-on file listing or copy operations.

tuning.description: Minimum number of unique destination hosts over SMB within TimeWindow to treat as scanning (e.g., ≥5).
Correlation window between the discovery process start and SMB fan-out (default 10m).
Service/admin accounts legitimately running inventory scripts.
Pipes (e.g., \PIPE\spoolss) normally accessed by management agents; exclude from alerts.

log_sources.name: etw:Microsoft-Windows-RPC
log_sources.channel: rpc_call: srvsvc.NetShareEnum / NetShareEnumAll from non-admin or unusual processes

analytics.name: Analytic 0514
analytics.guidance: CLI tools (smbclient -L, smbmap, rpcclient, nmblookup) or custom scripts enumerate SMB shares on many internal hosts → corresponding SMB connections (445/139) captured by Zeek/Netflow within a short window.

tuning.description: Correlation window between tool exec and SMB fan-out (default 10m).
IPs of vulnerability scanners or config mgmt systems.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve of smbclient, smbmap, rpcclient, nmblookup, crackmapexec smb

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: connection: TCP connections to ports 139/445 to multiple hosts

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: smb_command: TreeConnectAndX to \\*\IPC$ / srvsvc or Trans2/NT_CREATE for listing shares

analytics.name: Analytic 0515
analytics.guidance: Use of native/mac tools (sharing -l, smbutil view, mount_smbfs) or scripts to enumerate SMB shares across many hosts, followed by outbound SMB connections observed in PF/Zeek logs.

tuning.description: Minimum unique SMB destinations (e.g., ≥3–5 in smaller mac fleets).
Correlation window between exec and SMB connections (default 10m).

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Command line contains smbutil view //, mount_smbfs //

log_sources.name: NSM:Firewall
log_sources.channel: Outbound connections to 139/445 to multiple destinations

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: connection: SMB connections to multiple internal hosts

[Reference](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-136a)
